Google Reports Strong Revenue but Sees Stock Drop After Admitting AI Search Yields Lower Margins

30 Oct 2026, 09:28 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Tech Desk · Source: arstechnica.com

Image: arstechnica.com — Creative Commons

Key takeawaysAlphabet, the parent company of Google, released its third-quarter financial results for 2026, revealing substantial overall revenue growth alongside a significant drop in its stock price. While the tech giant brought in nearly $128 billion during the July-to-September

Alphabet, the parent company of Google, released its third-quarter financial results for 2026, revealing substantial overall revenue growth alongside a significant drop in its stock price. While the tech giant brought in nearly $128 billion during the July-to-September period, market reaction was sharply negative due to escalating artificial intelligence expenditures and lower revenue yields from AI-driven search queries.

Financial Performance and Market Reaction

Google reported a net income of more than $26 billion for Q3 2026, with overall revenue up 25 percent compared to the same period in the previous year. However, net income fell roughly $9 billion lower than prior figures, and earnings per share came in at $2.12, falling short of analyst consensus projections of $3.02.

Following the earnings announcement, Alphabet's stock price experienced a steep decline, dropping nearly 12 percent. Analysts and investors focused heavily on the company's surging capital expenditures, which reached $51.4 billion in Q3, contributing to a negative cash flow of $9.06 billion driven largely by infrastructure spending.

The Monetization Challenge of AI Search

During the company's earnings call, Chief Business Officer Philipp Schindler addressed the shifting dynamics of user search behavior. While overall search volume grew by 12 percent year-over-year, that growth rate slowed compared to previous quarters, which saw 17 percent growth in Q2 and 19 percent in Q1.

More critically, Schindler acknowledged that individual queries handled by Google's AI Mode generate less revenue than traditional web searches. These AI interactions currently feature fewer advertisements, and those ads cost less to run. To address the margin gap, Google announced plans to expand contextual advertising within AI Mode across additional international markets and introduce multi-turn ads in the United States, where sponsored links adapt dynamically as users engage in back-and-forth conversations with the chatbot.

Cloud Growth and Future Spending Plans

Despite headwinds in search monetization, Google's Cloud products surpassed analyst expectations by generating over $30 billion in revenue, more than doubling over the past year. Company executives pointed to strong demand for AI compute infrastructure—utilized by external startups and major AI firms alike—as justification for continued financial commitment.

Alphabet confirmed that it expects total 2026 spending to land between $195 billion and $205 billion, with preliminary targets exceeding $300 billion in AI investments for 2027.

Practical Implications and Verification

What Is Confirmed

  • Alphabet reported Q3 2026 revenue of nearly $128 billion and net income exceeding $26 billion.
  • Capital expenditures reached $51.4 billion in Q3, resulting in a negative cash flow of $9.06 billion.
  • Google executives confirmed that AI search queries currently yield lower ad revenue per query than traditional web searches.
  • The company plans to expand contextual and multi-turn advertising within AI Mode.

What Remains Unknown

  • Whether advertisers will ultimately value AI search ads at rates comparable to traditional search inventory.
  • The long-term sustainability of external venture-backed spending on cloud AI infrastructure.

How to Verify

Readers can review the official financial disclosures and earnings transcripts directly via [Ars Technica's coverage of the Alphabet Q3 earnings report](https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2026/10/google-admits-ai-search-makes-less-money-but-its-fixing-that-with-more-ads/).
